newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may sell grain to new markets - Ag minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia may sell grain to new markets - Ag minister.

text.p: Russia may increase the volume of its grain exports to a wider range of countries in 1997 and 1998, Interfax news agency quoted Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun as saying on Monday.
Khlystun also said Russia would continue to import some grain for its Far Eastern regions, including maize (corn) and soymeal, as it has been doing in the past.
But he said maize imports would be sharply down following a good domestic crop. He gave no further details on imports.
Russian grain exports would include rye, wheat for human consumption and several kinds of cereals.
Khlystun said Russia, which has in the past exported mainly to the former Soviet republics in Central Asia and the Caucasus, was now considering entering new, unspecified markets.
He said it was too early to predict the 1997 harvest's volume but that this year's crop could outperform last year's significantly.
The 1996 net grain harvest was officially 69.3 million tonnes, one of the worst on record in 30 years.
Officials have said output this year will be 70-70 million tonnes, with First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and the Grain Union predicting 80 million tonnes.
Russia is still a small net grain importer and still relies on overseas products to meet around 40 percent of its total food needs.
Khlystun said the grain-belt Krasnodar region could see its grains crops rise by one million tonnes to 5.4-5.5 million tonnes, while Tatarstan could produce a record-high crop.
He also said Russia could export leftovers from last year's stock of grain, which amounted to three million tonnes.
